sn1.11:3.3: _Naradeva_ is a term for a king. Here and at [sn9.6:4.3]() it refers to the gods of the Thirty-Three, and at [thag20.1:41.1]() to Brahmā. At [cp5:1.3]() it apparently refers to the aristocrats who are “gods among men” (see Manu 11.82).
sn1.11:3.4: _Tidasa_ (“thirty”) is a poetic abbreviation for the “thirty-three” gods.
sn1.11:5.1: The vocative form _bāle_ suggests that a female deity is being addressed, which is certainly the case in the parallel passage at [sn9.6:5.1]().
sn1.11:5.3: This famous verse, which occurs many times in the Suttas, was spoken by the Buddha at [sn15.20:8.2]() and by Sakka, the lord of the thirty-three, at the Buddha’s passing ([sn6.15:6.2](), [dn16:6.10.11](). | The unusual reading _sabbasaṅkhārā_ (rather than _vata saṅkhārā_) recurs in the parallel passage at [sn9.6:5.3]().
